title: When the square-root shortcut fails
promptMarkdown: A hypothetical monoprotic acid has $K_a=1.00\times10^{-4}$ at $25^\circ\mathrm C$. Its analytical concentration is $0.0100\,\mathrm M$. Derive the mass and charge balances under the approximation that water ionisation is negligible. Compute $h$ using both $\sqrt{K_aC}$ and the positive quadratic root, then pH and percentage ionisation. Quantify the error in the shortcut and justify whether neglect of water was consistent.
hintLadder: Write both conserved acid concentration and electrical neutrality.
Solve the quadratic before deciding which root is physical.
Compare the computed dissociation with the original analytical concentration.
